title: Function Signature and Data Flow
definition: A function signature exposes a callable interface, while data flow describes how explicit input values become local parameters and how results return to later expressions.
purpose: Design small composable interfaces and make transformations traceable across calls.
history: Signatures and composition support modular reasoning; exact signature definitions and type information vary by language and notation.
mental_model: Data moves through a pipeline: arguments enter named positions, the function transforms them, and a returned value becomes the next stage's argument.
analogy: A pipeline with labeled connectors; it fails when effects, shared state, errors, or aliasing create additional channels.
common_mistakes: Mixing query and hidden command effects
industry_notes: Composition requires compatible contracts, not merely syntactically nestable calls.
ai_notes: Require a data-flow diagram and contract compatibility check for AI-generated pipelines.
interview_notes: Ask when to group related inputs and how return design affects composition.
